The team's mascot is a black swallow with a red face named Tsubakuro (つば九郎, *Tsubakurō*). He is known for his feuds with the [Orix Buffaloes](/wiki/Orix_Buffaloes "Orix Buffaloes")' mascots. He always wears a batting helmet. Whenever the Swallows wear special home uniforms, Tsubakuro also wears the same.

The number on the back of his uniform is "2896" as opposed to 111/222 used by [Buffalo Bull and Buffalo Bell](/wiki/Orix_Buffaloes#Mascots "Orix Buffaloes"), the Buffaloes' mascots.

There is also a female swallow mascot named Tsubami. She wears a skirt and may be intended as Tsubakuro's little sister, just as Bell is Bull's little sister. Unlike her brother, she wears a sports visor.

Before Tsubakuro was created, the team's mascots were Yabo (ヤー坊, *Yābō*) and Sue-chan (スーちゃん, *Sū-chan*), who were the team mascots from 1979 to 1994.

The team also had a third mascot named Torcuya (トルクーヤ, *Torukūya*), a swallow who resembles a [luchador](/wiki/Luchador "Luchador"). He always carries around a parasol and a bottle of Yakult that he carries on his back.

The team also had a former mascot named Entaro (燕太郎, *Entarō*), a swallow who wore a jersey with the number 8960. He was replaced by Torcuya in 2014.

The Swallows farm team plays in the [Eastern League](/wiki/Eastern_League_(Japanese_baseball) "Eastern League (Japanese baseball)"). The team was founded in 1950.

Most sets were a combination of practical sets and [chroma key](/wiki/Chroma_key "Chroma key") backgrounds. For example, in the Glass Stepping Stones scenes, the set, designed as if in a circus tent for the players performing for the VIPs, was only 1.5 metres (4.9 ft) off the ground, using chroma key screens to simulate the height in post-production. In filming, this was far enough from the ground to make the actors nervous, which contributed to the scene.[[95]](#cite_note-collider_bts-102)[[94]](#cite_note-variety_production-101) The tug-of-war set was actually set more than 10 metres (33 ft) off the ground, which further created anxiety for some of the actors with fears of heights.[[94]](#cite_note-variety_production-101)

The robot doll in the first episode, "Red Light, Green Light", was inspired by Young-hee, a character who appeared on the covers of South Korean textbooks *Chul-soo and Young-hee* in the 1970s and 1980s,[[92]](#cite_note-arch_digest-99) and her hairstyle was inspired by Hwang's daughter's.[[91]](#cite_note-doll-98)[[94]](#cite_note-variety_production-101) The doll singsongs, in Korean, "Mugunghwa flower has blossomed", referring to the *[Hibiscus syriacus](/wiki/Hibiscus_syriacus "Hibiscus syriacus")*, the [national flower](/wiki/National_flower "National flower") of South Korea.[[67]](#cite_note-nbcnews_games-73) The use of this familiar character was meant to juxtapose memories of childhood and unsettling fear in the players, according to Chae.[[94]](#cite_note-variety_production-101) Similarly, the set for the dalgona game, using giant pieces of playground equipment, were to evoke players' memories of their childhood, and was a common place where South Korean children would have played dalgona with friends.[[94]](#cite_note-variety_production-101) The [dalgona](/wiki/Dalgona "Dalgona") used in "The Man with the Umbrella" were made by a street vendor from [Daehangno](/wiki/Daehangno "Daehangno").[[96]](#cite_note-103)

The [Log College](/wiki/Log_College "Log College"), an influential aspect of Princeton's development

Princeton University, founded as the College of New Jersey, was shaped much in its formative years by the "[Log College](/wiki/Log_College "Log College")", a [seminary](/wiki/Seminary "Seminary") founded by the Reverend [William Tennent](/wiki/William_Tennent "William Tennent") at [Neshaminy, Pennsylvania](/wiki/Neshaminy,_Pennsylvania "Neshaminy, Pennsylvania"), in about 1726. While no legal connection ever existed, many of the pupils and adherents from the Log College would go on to financially support and become substantially involved in the early years of the university.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeitch1978291–292-14) While early writers considered it as the predecessor of the university,[[18]](#cite_note-Holland-1877-19) the idea has been rebuked by Princeton historians.[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeitch1978291–292-14)

The founding of the university itself originated from a split in the [Presbyterian](/wiki/Presbyterianism "Presbyterianism") church following the [Great Awakening](/wiki/Great_Awakening "Great Awakening").[[20]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOberdorfer199511-21) In 1741, [New Light](/wiki/Old_Side%E2%80%93New_Side_Controversy "Old Side–New Side Controversy") Presbyterians were expelled from the [Synod of Philadelphia](/wiki/Synod_of_Philadelphia "Synod of Philadelphia") in defense of how the Log College ordained ministers.[[21]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeitch1978198-22) The four founders of the College of New Jersey, who were New Lights, were either expelled or withdrew from the Synod and devised a plan to establish a new college, for they were disappointed with [Harvard](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") and [Yale](/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University")'s opposition to the Great Awakening and dissatisfied with the limited instruction at the Log College.[[21]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeitch1978198-22)[[20]](#cite_note-FOO

Several foods and dietary supplements have been associated with lung cancer risk. High consumption of some animal products – [red meat](/wiki/Red_meat "Red meat") (but not other meats or fish), [saturated fats](/wiki/Saturated_fat "Saturated fat"), as well as [nitrosamines](/wiki/Nitrosamine "Nitrosamine") and [nitrites](/wiki/Nitrite "Nitrite") (found in salted and smoked meats) – is associated with an increased risk of developing lung cancer.[[94]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBadeDela_Cruz2020"Diet"-94) In contrast, high consumption of fruits and vegetables is associated with a reduced risk of lung cancer, particularly consumption of [cruciferous vegetables](/wiki/Cruciferous_vegetables "Cruciferous vegetables") and raw fruits and vegetables.[[94]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBadeDela_Cruz2020"Diet"-94) Based on the beneficial effects of fruits and vegetables, supplementation of several individual vitamins have been studied. Supplementation with [vitamin A](/wiki/Vitamin_A "Vitamin A") or [beta-carotene](/wiki/Beta-carotene "Beta-carotene") had no effect on lung cancer, and instead slightly increased mortality.[[94]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBadeDela_Cruz2020"Diet"-94) Dietary supplementation with [vitamin E](/wiki/Vitamin_E "Vitamin E") or [retinoids](/wiki/Retinoid "Retinoid") similarly had no effect.[[95]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBadeDela_Cruz2020"Chemopreventive_Agents"-95) Consumption of [polyunsaturated fats](/wiki/Polyunsaturated_fat "Polyunsaturated fat"), tea, alcoholic beverages, and coffee are all associated with reduced risk of developing lung cancer.[[94]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBadeDela_Cruz2020"Diet"-94)

[The House of the Government of the Russian Federation](/wiki/White_House_(Moscow) "White House (Moscow)")

In Moscow, as in a city endowed with the [Constitution of the Russian Federation](/wiki/Constitution_of_Russia "Constitution of Russia"), the legislative, executive, and judicial federal authorities of the country are located, with the exception of the [Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation](/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Russia "Constitutional Court of Russia"), which has been located in [Saint Petersburg](/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg") since 2008.

The supreme executive authority – the [Government of the Russian Federation](/wiki/Government_of_Russia "Government of Russia") – is located in the House of the Government of the Russian Federation (the [White House](/wiki/White_House_(Moscow) "White House (Moscow)")) on [Krasnopresnenskaya Embankment](/wiki/Krasnopresnenskaya_Embankment "Krasnopresnenskaya Embankment") in the center of Moscow. The [State Duma](/wiki/State_Duma "State Duma") sits on [Okhotny Ryad](/wiki/Okhotny_Ryad_(street) "Okhotny Ryad (street)"). The [Federation Council](/wiki/Federation_Council_(Russia) "Federation Council (Russia)") is located in a building on [Bolshaya Dmitrovka](/wiki/Bolshaya_Dmitrovka_Street "Bolshaya Dmitrovka Street"). The [Supreme Court of the Russian Federation](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Russia "Supreme Court of Russia") is also located in Moscow.

The [Moscow Kremlin](/wiki/Moscow_Kremlin "Moscow Kremlin") is the official residence of the President of the Russian Federation. The president's working residence in the Kremlin is located in the [Senate Palace](/wiki/Kremlin_Senate "Kremlin Senate").
